**Course source:** Day 3 §4.3–§4.6. The running application contains Product, Order and User services.

## Instrumentation and storage are different roles

The source pairs **Spring Cloud Sleuth** for instrumentation/context propagation with **Zipkin** for collecting and visualising traces. A tracer creates spans inside services; a collector receives them; a backend stores them; a UI helps inspect them.

~~~text
Gateway / Order / Product
    -> tracing instrumentation
    -> exporter -> Zipkin collector
    -> query/search UI
~~~

The collector cannot infer spans that applications never generated. A service that does not propagate context may appear as an unrelated trace even if it sends data to the same backend.

## Example: find a slow Product call

A user reports a 1-second checkout. Search by a known trace ID or time window, then inspect the longest child span. If Product's client span occupies most of the request, investigate Product's downstream database or network. If there is a large gap outside spans, instrumentation may be incomplete.

A trace answers **where time was spent**, not necessarily **why** a query was slow. Combine it with logs and metrics.

## Storage and sampling matter

Recording every span for very high traffic can be expensive. Sampling reduces volume but may lose rare failures unless policy is designed carefully. Trace retention should fit debugging needs and data protection obligations.

## Move beyond the old course wiring

Spring Cloud Sleuth's original API and integration are historical for newer Spring Boot generations. Prefer current Micrometer Tracing/OpenTelemetry instrumentation with an exporter compatible with Zipkin or another backend.

Use official up-to-date setup instructions instead of relying on old Maven dependencies or copied properties.

[Zipkin](https://zipkin.io/) · [Micrometer Tracing](https://micrometer.io/).

## Mathematical Abstraction

A distributed trace groups spans by shared trace identity.

$$
T_{\tau}=\{s\in S:\operatorname{traceId}(s)=\tau\}
$$

$\tau$ is the trace identifier. Context propagation is necessary for spans from different services to join the same logical trace.
